target_customer: Uninsured and cost-sensitive US consumers needing simple primary care
problem: Simple visits for birth control, UTIs and acne cost too much; HeyDoctor offered five minute app visits usually under $20 with no insurance needed.
business_model: Pay per visit telemedicine, later part of GoodRx

founders.name: Brendan Levy
founders.background_notes: Later executive medical director at GoodRx and then Clara Health per YC bio and press.

founders.name: Rohit Malhotra
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Levy's YC bio but not listed as active.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app with clinician workflow and state licensing logistics; no deep technology.

defensibility.rationale: State clinician licensing is a modest barrier; the visit model was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GoodRx acquired it in September 2019 and rebranded it GoodRx Care around 2021.

market_need_then: Press in November 2017 said HeyDoctor visits cost under $20, over 50% below leading online competitors, signalling price pain in telehealth.

rebrands.why: GoodRx said the new brand reflects wider treatment coverage and savings benefits; exact date unconfirmed

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly conversational name but no sourced brand impact; it was retired for GoodRx Care.

outcome_analysis: HeyDoctor launched a low price app in late 2017, joined YC in summer 2018 and was acquired by GoodRx in September 2019 to give GoodRx a telemedicine entry. The brand was relaunched as HeyDoctor by GoodRx and then GoodRx Care. The sale price is undisclosed, and the exit looks like a strategic fit rather than evidence of standalone scale.
